manifesto.title: OUR STUDENT MANIFESTO
manifesto.opening: We will represent these student needs before the university and work for their implementation.

points.title: NEED-BASED HOSTEL QUOTA
points.text: Advocate for a separate hostel quota for financially disadvantaged students who miss the academic merit cutoff, so financial hardship is considered in hostel allotment.

points.title: BETTER CLASSROOM FACILITIES
points.text: Seek smartboards, sliding writing boards, projectors, and adequate tables and desks for classrooms.

points.title: DRINKING WATER, SANITATION AND MENSTRUAL HYGIENE
points.text: Work for sufficient, regularly maintained water coolers and safe drinking water; clean washrooms with reliable water supply and proper hygiene facilities; and sanitary pad vending machines with designated facilities for safe disposal of used pads.

points.title: STUDENT SUGGESTION BOXES
points.text: Introduce suggestion boxes so students can share concerns and ideas, with regular review and follow-up.

points.title: WELL-EQUIPPED CENTRAL CANTEEN
points.text: Seek a hygienic central canteen with adequate facilities and separate seating areas for students and staff.

points.title: SPORTS AND INTERDEPARTMENTAL EVENTS
points.text: Work for adequate sports equipment and regular interdepartmental sports competitions.

points.title: TECHNICAL AND SKILL DEVELOPMENT
points.text: Organise webinars, workshops, technical tests, and hackathons, and support active tech clubs for practical learning.

points.title: INNOVATION CLUB AND PROJECT FUNDING
points.text: Support students with creative and technical ideas through an innovation club. Seek sponsorship, grants, and institutional funding to help turn promising ideas into projects.

points.title: SCIENCE, HUMANITIES AND CULTURAL CLUB
points.text: Promote science and humanities activities alongside social literacy, community service, dance, singing, and other cultural programmes.

points.title: INCUBATION AND STARTUP COLLABORATION
points.text: Work towards an incubation club where students can discuss collaborative ideas with startups and seek mentorship and funding from the university or other institutions.

points.title: COLLEGE-FUNDED EDUCATIONAL TOURS
points.text: Advocate for college-funded academic, cultural, industrial, and study tours, both within the state and outside it.

points.title: LABORATORY UPGRADATION
points.text: Seek upgraded laboratories with reliable internet, suitable cabins or workspaces, projectors, desktops, and designated bag storage.

points.title: LIBRARY UPGRADATION
points.text: Work for air-conditioned library facilities and an expanded collection of relevant textbooks, reference books, and updated learning materials.

points.title: HEALTHCARE UPGRADATION
points.text: Advocate for improved campus healthcare, including diagnostic facilities, essential medicines, and timely treatment.

points.title: CLEAR, BILINGUAL QUESTION PAPERS
points.text: Seek question papers printed on standard A4 sheets with readable font sizes, replacing cramped or miniature printing. Advocate for questions in both Urdu and English.

points.title: CIVIL ENGINEERING: PRACTICAL AND SOFTWARE LEARNING
points.text: Advocate for software-integrated coursework, varied locations for surveying practicals, and construction-site visits every Saturday.

points.title: ECE: INDUSTRY-RELEVANT EQUIPMENT
points.text: Seek current, industry-relevant chips and development hardware, along with a VLSI test bed for practical learning.

points.title: RELIABLE WI-FI IN THE SCHOOL OF ENGINEERING AND TECHNOLOGY
points.text: Take up poor connectivity with the administration and work for stronger Wi-Fi coverage and reliable internet across classrooms, laboratories, and student activity spaces.
